name: audio-2
note: The audio examples of the shelf: three spoken pieces played by a wave player (no picture, no video: the sound is an MP3 and the page draws the wave from 96 slices of its loudness kept in the catalogue) in three domains and three languages (a business update in English, an audiobook page in Spanish, the summary of a technical document in Chinese), then the two films of the first audio lot that were kept (guided breathing, bedtime story), then a card of text only (`card: "prompt"`): the summary of a ready-made prompt that a click puts straight into the composer, with no dialog. The voices are AI voices; the two examples in the maintainer's own cloned voice of lot 1 were dropped. `hue` is the colour of the wave. `request` is what the example's button puts in the composer; `made.prompt` is the text the voice read.

entry.name: Quarterly update, read aloud
entry.line: A board update turned into a clear voice you can send to the team.
entry.alt: A modern wave player on a blue gradient, playing a spoken business update

cells.request: Turn this quarterly update into a 20-second audio brief for my team, in a clear, confident English voice: revenue up 18 percent led by subscriptions, churn down to 2.1 percent, onboarding cut from nine days to three, support volume doubled. Give me the audio file and the text.

made.label: ElevenLabs v4
made.prompt: Good morning, everyone. Here is the quarter in one minute. Revenue grew eighteen percent, led by subscriptions, and churn fell to two point one percent. The new onboarding cut the time to first value from nine days to three. One risk to watch: support volume, which doubled.

cells.source: voice ElevenLabs v4 through the AI gateway (Brian), trimmed, loudness -16 LUFS, MP3 128 kbit/s; the figures are invented for the sample

entry.name: Two-host podcast from a document
entry.line: Two hosts talk through your document: a hook, three key points with an example each, a short recap. About 3 minutes, in a natural voice.

cells.request: Turn the document I attach into a 3-minute two-host podcast episode. Host A is curious and asks the questions, host B explains. Structure: a 15-second hook, three key points each with one concrete example, then a 20-second recap and one question for the listener. Natural spoken English, short sentences, light humour, no jargon. Warm studio voices, a different voice for each host, a soft intro and outro. Before generating, show me the script and the voices you picked; then give me the MP3 and the transcript.
